newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia air technicians to strike, delays seen.
newsitem.headline: Colombia air technicians to strike, delays seen.

text.p: Colombia's airport technicians, responsible for navigation and radar systems, will join the national public sector strike due to begin Tuesday, with an "inevitable" delay of all flights and in some cases cancellations, air traffic controllers said.

Air traffic controllers will not join the industrial action, which is expected to be backed by about 800,000 state workers, but said they will have to apply special safety norms which will lead to a backlog of national and international air traffic.

"The decision to join the strike is taken. We will define the exact mechanisms of our participation in the strike in a meeting later today," said Oscar Garca, head of the Colombian Airport Technicians Association.
All airports will be affected by the strike, he said, including the country's main international airports in Bogota, Cali, and Medellin.

"In view of the technicians' strike and because of international safety norms we will have to apply a greater separation of flight plans," said Csar Valle, spokesman for the Association of Colombian Air Traffic Controllers. "We will not be going on strike ourselves because of our role as an essential public service. But the safety measures will mean delays in all national and international flights of between one and two hours. Towards Tuesday afternoon and evening with a backlog of flights we may have to cancel some services," he added.

State workers have called the strike to press for a wage hike of about 21.5 percent compared to the government pay rise offer of a weighted 13.5 percent. They are also protesting at the whittling away of labor rights and government plans for the privatization of national and regional industries.
